author: opt-W1

contract.sync_assumed: none beyond warp convergence of the logical warp's lanes
contract.type_constraints: bf16 keys packed into one 32-bit word (key bits high, inverted 16-bit index low, N at most 65536), fp32 keys packed into one 64-bit word (key bits high, inverted 32-bit index low), int32 source indices derived from the striped position
contract.nan_behavior: a NaN key orders by its sign bit (positive NaN above every finite key, negative NaN below), deterministic, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 is mapped to +0.0 before packing so the two zeros compare equal
contract.tie_break_support: inherent in the word order: among equal keys the smaller index gives the larger word, prefer_smaller_index costs nothing (psi cells equal the ng cells to the cycle, same code)
contract.sorted_output_support: inherent: the first k striped positions are sorted by (key descending, index ascending)
contract.k_range: [1, MaxK] with MaxK = round_up(k, LW), N / MaxK a power of two, LW the logical warp size 4, 8 or 16
contract.n_range: N a multiple of LW with N / MaxK a power of two, measured 8, 16, 32 and 128 (bf16 N at most 65536)

correctness_notes: Oracle battery passed in every cell for both requirements. Control W1_packed_sub (CUB eager, same packed words, same logical warp size) in the same lock section for both requirements. Built against the shared harness at swarm commit b6bfae9a37bb, sources at W1 worktree commit 851d41cc5c. The first measurement (batch W1_level_sub_vs_W1_packed_sub_focus_kill_n2_20261025_131831.json, commit ccc1166d9c) had the word array in local memory in 30 of 116 TUs at N 128 (T36) and is superseded by this card, the unaffected cells agree to the cycle. Two W1 optimizer instances shared one agent id on 2026-10-25. This card is Instance A (opt-W1, worktree cccl-topk-swarm-W1, branch exp/topk-swarm/W1): the N2 verdict here is W1_level against W1_packed (the CUB eager network on the same packed words). Instance B (opt-W1b) owns the same-code eager against level comparison with min max stages and the fp32 native min max pairs variant (cards W1_eager_same, W1_level_pairs, W1_minmax_pairs on B200), report approaches/W1/REPORT_W1b.md.

low_level: Registers of the latency kernel: bf16 29 to 57 up to N 32, 64 to 71 at LW 8 and 16 N 128, 96 to 99 at LW 4 N 128 (32 words per lane plus the harness's 32 keys and indices). fp32 33 to 64 up to N 32, 64 to 95 at LW 8 and 16 N 128, 126 to 168 at LW 4 N 128. Throughput kernel at most 64 registers (bf16) and 128 (fp32 LW 4 N 128), occupancy 8 blocks per SM down to 4 at LW 4 and 8 N 128 and 2 for fp32 LW 4 N 128. The only nonzero stack frames left are 8 bytes with 12 bytes of spill in the 64-register throughput kernel of bf16 LW 4 N 128 k 8 and 16, honest spills, not local arrays.

The sub-warp eager chain at LW 4 and MaxK 4 is 32 tiles at N 128 (2 shuffle stages per sort, 2 per merge), the level form sorts all 32 at once (2 stages at IPT 32) and then 5 levels, 1819 against 2668 cycles bf16, 2627 against 3369 fp32. At LW 16 N 128 k 4 (MaxK 16, 8 tiles) 888 against 3504 (3.95x) and 2297 against 4033 (1.76x).
No-op control slope 87 to 109 cycles per call at sub-warp scope (48 at warp), R squared 1.0000 on every fit, canaries 32.001 cycles per op and 3609 to 3611 us at start and end of the section.
Instruction mix as at warp scope: two predicated VIMNMX per exchange for bf16, compare and selects for fp32 u64, no branch inside the network (BRA equals the no-op kernel's count).
algorithmic: bf16 against the eager form on the same words, latency: LW 4 1.47x to 3.04x (N 8 k 4 185 against 296, N 32 k 8 421 against 1279, N 128 k 64 2952 against 6971), LW 8 1.28x to 3.77x (N 16 k 4 302 against 422, N 32 k 16 441 against 1175, N 128 k 8 1074 against 4050), LW 16 1.17x to 4.19x (N 16 366 against 428, N 32 k 8 466 against 809, N 128 k 64 1053 against 4410). The gain grows with the tile count N / MaxK as the model says: 1.2x to 1.7x at two tiles, 2x to 3x at four to eight, 3.4x to 4.2x at eight to sixteen tiles of 8 or 16 lanes.

fp32 (u64 words): LW 4 1.28x to 2.37x, LW 8 1.09x to 1.49x, LW 16 0.96x to 1.76x (N 32 k 16 853 against 816 is the one loss, two tiles). The u64 register stages at MaxK above LW (k 16 and 64 at LW 4 and 8, M 2 to 16 words per tile) keep the fp32 gains below the bf16 ones.

Throughput: bf16 LW 8 and 16 1.14x to 1.47x, fp32 LW 8 and 16 1.05x to 1.33x at N at least 16, LW 4 0.91x to 1.08x for both types: at LW 4 the throughput kernel is register bound (64 to 128 registers, 4 or 2 blocks per SM) and the level form's higher register footprint costs what its ALU saving gains.

The focus cells of the W1 card: sub-warp LW 8 N 16 k 4 (DBRX and gpt-oss-20b routing shape) bf16 302 cycles against 422 eager packed and 570 for the pairs reference in the same session (1.89x chained), fp32 523 against 600 and 516. LW 16 N 32 k 8 bf16 466 against 809 and 829 (1.78x chained), fp32 832 against 833 and 737.
prefer_smaller_index free in every cell (psi equals ng to the cycle).
negative: No throughput gain at LW 4 (0.91x to 1.08x): the level form keeps all N / LW words live through phase 1 while the eager form's register footprint is the current tile plus the retained one, so at 32 words per lane the occupancy drops and the ALU saving is spent.
fp32 LW 16 N 32 k 16 (two tiles of 16 words, M 1): 0.96x, the two-tile case loses for u64 as at warp scope.
surprises: The largest gains of the whole W1 study are here: 3.7x to 4.2x at LW 8 and 16 N 128 bf16, where the eager chain of 8 to 16 tiny sorts is pure dependency and the level form runs them all in the shadow of one.

The k-dependent schedule swing (T28) appears in the level form at sub-warp scope for fp32 (LW 16 N 128: 2297 at k 4 and 8, 3282 at k 16, same MaxK 16 network) and in the eager control for bf16 (LW 4 N 32: 772 at k 4, 1279 at k 8, 838 at k 16, MaxK 4, 8 and 16 are different networks there). T28's rule to measure every (N, k) instantiation separately holds at sub-warp scope too.
open_questions: Would keeping only the surviving tiles live (phase 1 in two halves, each followed by its levels, then one more level) recover the LW 4 throughput without losing the latency gain? The latency cost is one extra level of log2(MaxK) stages.

At LW 4 and 8 the sort of a 4 or 8 item tile is 2 or 3 shuffle stages, is a redux based or ballot based rank (T4, T19) cheaper than the network for MaxK at most 8 when the input has 16 or more tiles? W2's round is 26 cycles at IPT up to 8 (T19).
